title: Creative work counts when its reasoning shows
statement: Count a creative or performance product as evidence of reading only when its reasoning is inspectable, for instance through an attached justification of its choices from the text.
detail: An editorial synthesis of pandemic-era English cases, which records what was planned or offered rather than measured gains, takes from a secondary English self-study that included Grade 9 creative work the rule to treat a creative product as evidence only when its reading and reasoning are inspectable (`g9/library/collections/codex-2026-10-02-curriculum-research/COVID-ERA-TEACHING-EVIDENCE.md`, lines 21 and 26). It also asks that writing and source use be made observable through drafts, quotations, revision and oral explanation (line 39). The research pack's teaching page names the risk of performance and making as engaging production without analysis, checked by whether pupils can explain what a choice reveals (`g9/library/text/L0a378f.txt`, line 1), and notes on a student performance task attach a short justification of why a line was said that way, so it is gradable on textual grounds, not just performance flair (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/video-04-student-performance-gallery.md`, lines 102-104).
against: "A school plan, platform guide or first-person reflection establishes a practice or intention, not its effectiveness." (`g9/library/collections/codex-2026-10-02-curriculum-research/COVID-ERA-TEACHING-EVIDENCE.md`, line 45): the rule rests on documented cases, not a measured outcome.

so it is gradable on textual grounds, not just performance flair.
